title: Celery, Silverbeet and Goat's Cheese Bechamel Lasagne
subtitle: a vegetarian lasagne with root vegetables
description: A vegetarian lasagne layered with a celery, celeriac and silverbeet filling and a goat's cheese bechamel. Adding water around the edges before baking keeps the pasta sheets evenly cooked.

steps.text: Make the bechamel: melt 60 g of the butter in a pot over medium heat and add the flour. Stir the roux for a few minutes until it starts to brown. Gradually add the milk, whisking constantly.
Keep cooking for a few minutes over low heat until thickened. Remove from the heat, strain, and add the goat's cheese to the hot bechamel.
Wait for the cheese to melt and stir until smooth.

Make the filling: heat the olive oil in a pot and fry the thinly sliced onion until translucent. Add the chopped celery stalks and leaves, thinly sliced peeled celeriac, garlic and finely chopped silverbeet. Add the wine and cook until the liquid reduces. Reduce the heat, add the remaining 80 g butter, season with salt and pepper and stir. Cool to room temperature.

Preheat the oven to 160°C. Grease a baking dish and lay a layer of lasagne sheets on the bottom (no pre-cooking needed). Top with a thin layer of filling and a little bechamel. Repeat the layers twice more, finishing with a layer of bechamel, and arrange the sliced mozzarella on top.
Pour 1/2 cup water around the edges of the lasagne, as close to the sides of the dish as possible, and bake for about 40 minutes until browned.
